988, 911, and Quick exit stay on every screen, at every age.

A safety plan lists signs that a hard moment is coming, what helps, who to contact, and your reasons for living. It helps most when you make it, or go over it, with a doctor or counselor.

Anyone who can unlock this phone can open the app. Quick exit leaves fast. Nobody at Tidelight sees what you write, so it isn't a way to ask for help. In a crisis, call or text 988, or call 911.

If this phone's iCloud or Google backup is on, the backup includes it. Delete everything, in Your journey, removes it from the phone now. A copy in an earlier backup can last until the phone's next backup.

If you choose to send it, this message goes to your people through the phone's own Messages app, with a map link to where you are. You see it first and tap Send yourself; the app can't send a text on its own. You can change the words now.
If you ever think about hurting yourself, tell an adult right away, or call or text 988.
If you'd like a plan for hard moments, make it with a trusted adult or a counselor, not alone.

If you're helping a child with this app: ask how they're feeling, listen without judging, keep anything that could hurt them out of reach, help them reach help, and check in again later. If a child says they're thinking about suicide or hurting themselves, stay with them and call or text 988. In immediate danger, call 911.
If you're under 13, please use Tidelight with a parent, carer, or another adult you trust.
